$comment: E2E SAS-MODE0 cross-surface contract vectors (RESUME-PROTOCOL RULE 30).
One file, two consumers: tests/e2e-sas-blocking-contract.test.mjs (web: hooks/phoneE2e.ts decideAccept ->
the view hooks/useE2e.ts publishes -> lib/encryptedModeCopy.ts sasIsBlocking + encryptionIndicator) and
Rows are the SPEC 13.2 cells: {phone encrypted mode OFF|ON} x {computer encrypted mode OFF|ON} x
{a usable e2e block present|absent}. `blockPresent:false` is the pre-feature peer (E2eSettings
PeerAdvertisement.ABSENT): a side whose OWN setting is ON refuses rather than downgrades.
THE ROW THIS FILE EXISTS FOR IS row-4-M1: both sides OFF, block present. The pair SEALS (web view
mode:'on'), the EFFECTIVE mode stays OFF, digits are computed (frozen transcript + coverage) and NOBODY
IS ASKED TO CONFIRM THEM. Both surfaces must say 'Encrypted, unverified' and NEITHER may block on a SAS.
Web regression 2026-09-23 (live acceptance 3e466fd finding 2): sasIsBlocking keyed on view.mode (the
SEALING flag, 'on' for every sealed pair) and opened the modal over the whole panel.
`effective` on the web abort rows is what decideAccept actually returns on the no-block abort path
(mode 'on' / effective 'on' / state 'error'); it is recorded verbatim so the test pins the real path.

rows.label: phone OFF, computer OFF, no e2e block (pre-feature peer)
phone OFF, computer ON, no e2e block — the computer refuses rather than downgrades
phone ON, computer OFF, no e2e block — the phone refuses rather than downgrades
phone OFF, computer OFF, block present — SEALED at modeByte 0x00, effective OFF, SAS NOT blocking on either side
phone OFF, computer ON, block present — the OR makes it verified; the locally-OFF phone still confirms
phone ON, computer OFF, block present — the OR makes it verified; the locally-OFF computer still confirms
phone ON, computer ON, block present — verified on both ends, SAS blocking on both ends
phone ON, computer ON, no e2e block — both sides refuse
